image_description: A Dungeness crab positioned on a white, slightly wrinkled fabric background. The crab is viewed from a high angle, showing its broad, oval carapace which is reddish-orange with some mottling. Two large claws (chelipeds) are visible at the front, and multiple walking legs extend laterally. The legs appear somewhat translucent or pale orange. The lighting is diffuse, casting soft shadows.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two claws are visible, but they appear relatively symmetrical in size rather than distinctly unequal. Furthermore, the tips are not clearly 'dark-tipped'; they are the same pale orange/white color as the rest of the claw, lacking the characteristic dark pigmentation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Claws have smooth outer surface and serrated inner edges.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The resolution is insufficient to definitively confirm serrated inner edges. The outer surface appears smooth, but the lack of clear definition on the inner margins makes this checkpoint fail strict verification.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The legs on the left side of the image appear to fuse into the carapace without distinct joint structures. One leg seems to emerge from an ambiguous point, lacking clear anatomical separation.

The legs have a waxy, semi-translucent appearance that differs significantly from the hard, opaque calcified texture of the carapace. They look somewhat like melted plastic or wax rather than biological chitin.
The distal end of the right-most visible walking leg appears to taper off into nothingness or blend into the background fabric without a clear tip or joint structure.
